title: Revenge Postponed: Team Pillbert Rolls Dawgs While Jayden Daniels Watches From the Bench
dek: Alan wins his fourth straight in Mekhi's revenge game, the HULK climbs to 55% title odds, Jordan finally gets on the board, and the top of the table is a three-way tie at 4-1.
body: Mekhi got the revenge game the schedule promised him, and Alan still walked out with the win. Team Pillbert beat Dawgs 143.66 to 108.44, the week's top score, behind Jahmyr Gibbs, who posted 35.2 points on a 24.57 projection for the best line in the league. The trade subplot went Mekhi's way on paper: Davante Adams scored 19.6 and Ashton Jeanty 9.2 for Dawgs, while Justin Jefferson gave Alan 15.8 in his debut. Kai won that exchange by 13 points and lost the game by 35.22, which is a strange way to collect a receipt.

The bigger wound was self-inflicted. Tyler Shough started at quarterback for Dawgs and finished with -0.16 points on a 16.51 projection, while Jayden Daniels sat on the bench with 32.26. That one swap is worth 32.42 points, just 2.8 shy of the final margin, and Christian Watson was also on the pine with 29.3 on an 11.52 projection. Mekhi kept grinding the wire anyway, adding Malik Nabers for TreVeyon Henderson, swapping the Ravens D/ST for the Bengals D/ST, and trading kicker Harrison Mevis for Will Reichard, but Dawgs are 1-4 with 25% playoff odds.

Ramon's No Banner only HULK beat Randy's The fumblers 134 to 99.64 as a 63% favorite. Josh Allen threw in 30.5 points on a 19.9 projection, and in the same week Brucie dropped the Bills D/ST to add T.J. Hockenson, which is about the most complicated loyalty move a Chicago-born Bills fan can make. Matthew Stafford scored 27.32 on the HULK's bench, and it barely mattered. The HULK now leads the league with 695 points, 70.5 more than anyone else, and its title odds jumped from 41% to 55%.

Randy got a monster game from Jaylen Warren, 33.8 points on a 15.86 projection, and it still wasn't close. The fumblers have dropped two straight, their title odds fell from 14% to 4%, and their playoff odds sit at a coin-flip 48%. The week on the wire was a boomerang: Randy dropped Trevor Lawrence for Deshaun Watson, then dropped Watson and picked Lawrence right back up, ending the week with the same quarterback and a little more mileage. He also cut Courtland Sutton, added Romeo Doubs, swapped the Rams D/ST for the Raiders D/ST, and replaced kicker Tyler Loop with Matt Gay.

Jordan finally got his first win, and he got it by the widest margin of the week. Counting or not Counting GV beat Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN 119.68 to 69.14 as a 43% underdog, a 50.54-point blowout led by Isaiah Likely's 26.9 in his first start after the trade with Alan. Jeremiyah Love's 2.2 on a 13.06 projection didn't matter, and Emeka Egbuka (14.2) and Denzel Boston (12.1) were on the bench, so JMoney actually had more in reserve. The playoff odds still read 1%, but the band finally got to play the fight song. For Zoe, Jared Goff delivered 28.94 on a 19.41 projection, which means the rest of the lineup combined for 40.2, the week's low score, and the rookie slides to 2-3 with 10% playoff odds.

Sonny's The Horse is Hea won at Habibsters 137.6 to 118.34, powered by Bucky Irving's 30.5 points on a 13.97 projection. Kaushal got 29.2 from Puka Nacua, but CeeDee Lamb went from last week's 32.8 to 1.9 on a 15.46 projection, the kind of deceleration nobody in Habibsters colors is known for. Habib is 1-4 despite 577.4 points, fourth-most in the league and more than 3-2 The fumblers, and his playoff odds are 30%. The commish's title odds climbed from 11% to 18%.

The standings have a familiar shape: No Banner only HULK, Team Pillbert, and The Horse is Hea are all 4-1, with playoff odds of 100%, 94%, and 93%. The odd detail is that Alan won his fourth straight and his title odds still fell from 21% to 16%, now behind Sonny's 18%, mostly because the HULK swallowed so much of the pie. The busiest desk again belonged to Philly, who added Joe Mixon and then dropped him, picked up Keon Coleman and Odell Beckham Jr., and made a new trade with Sonny: George Pickens and Ollie Gordon II go to The Horse is Hea, while Chuba Hubbard and DeVonta Smith go to Team Pillbert. Alan has now dealt with Randy, Jordan, Mekhi, and Sonny, which is half the league, and Sonny also swapped Tony Pollard for Emanuel Wilson.

Week 6 is headlined by The Horse is Hea against No Banner only HULK, a 4-1 versus 4-1 game where Sonny can either make it a race or watch Ramon pull away. Team Pillbert faces The fumblers, so Javonte Williams lines up against the team that traded him. Ghostu-Spider SZN hosts Dawgs with Zoe trying to get back to .500 and Mekhi trying to start the right quarterback, and Habibsters take on Counting or not Counting GV, where Jordan tries to make it two in a row against a team with far more points than its record shows.

trade_watch.take: Mekhi wins the scoreboard round of the revenge game: Adams and Jeanty combined for 28.8 in his lineup against Jefferson's 15.8 for Alan. But Alan won the actual game by 35.22, so this one is a points win for Dawgs and a standings win for Team Pillbert.

Week one is a landslide for Jordan: Isaiah Likely put up 26.9 in his first start to deliver the first win, with Egbuka and Boston adding 26.3 more from the bench. Alan got zero lineup points from Jeanty, who scored his 9.2 for Mekhi after being flipped right away.

It keeps getting worse for Randy. Javonte Williams added 13.2 as a starter and has 42 points for Alan, while Stefon Diggs didn't start and is still stuck on 6, a 36-point gap that will be on display when the teams meet next week.

This swap ends with both sides holding nothing: Hubbard leaves The Horse is Hea with 25.4 points scored and zero of them in Sonny's lineup, now shipped to Alan, and Rashee Rice still has zero points for the HULK. Two weeks in, it's a 0-0 tie that both managers would like to forget.

bios.1: Sonny's crew is 4-1 after Bucky Irving's 30.5 beat Habibsters, and the title odds jumped from 11% to 18%. A new trade brings Pickens and Ollie Gordon II on board just in time for a showdown with the HULK.
bios.2: Randy is 3-2 after two straight losses, with title odds down to 4% and playoff odds at 48%. Jaylen Warren's 33.8 wasn't enough, and a week of quarterback churn ended with Trevor Lawrence right back where he started.
bios.3: Jordan finally broke through with a 50.54-point win over Ghostu-Spider SZN, led by Isaiah Likely's 26.9. The 1-4 record and 1% playoff odds are steep, but the trade with Alan already looks like a smart rebuild.
bios.4: Alan has won four straight, and Gibbs's 35.2 steamrolled Dawgs in the revenge game. He has traded with half the league and holds 94% playoff odds, even as his title odds dipped to 16% in the HULK's shadow.
bios.5: Mekhi won the trade math in the revenge game but lost by 35.22, with Daniels and Watson combining for 61.56 on the bench. At 1-4 with 25% playoff odds, he keeps working the waiver wire, adding Malik Nabers this week.
bios.6: Kaushal is 1-4 but has the fourth-most points in the league at 577.4. Puka's 29.2 couldn't cover CeeDee's 1.9, and playoff odds of 30% say the two-time champ is still very much alive.
bios.7: Ramon's juggernaut is 4-1 with a league-best 695 points and has title odds of 55%, up from 41%. Josh Allen's 30.5 carried the win over The fumblers, and Stafford's 27.32 on the bench shows how deep this roster runs.
bios.8: Zoe's rookie season hit a wall with a league-low 69.14, even with Goff scoring 28.94. At 2-3 with 10% playoff odds, a home game against Dawgs is a chance to get back to .500.
